question.text: What is 'Gamma' and why is it important for option traders?

answer.text: Gamma measures the rate of change of delta per unit change in the underlying price — it indicates how quickly delta changes, effectively measuring the 'acceleration' of option price movement
Gamma measures the daily time decay of option premium
Gamma is the ratio of call premium to put premium for the same strike
Gamma only applies to deep out-of-the-money options

explanation.text: The Logic: Gamma is the change in an option's delta per unit change in the underlying price, so it acts as the 'acceleration' of delta. For example, if delta is 0.50 and gamma is 0.08, a Rs 1 rise in the underlying moves delta to roughly 0.58. The Trap: Time decay is measured by theta, not gamma, and gamma is not a ratio of call to put premium. The distractor about gamma applying only to deep OTM options confuses gamma with where it is largest. Note: Gamma is one of the standard option Greeks alongside delta, theta and vega, and is used by traders to gauge how stable an option's delta will be as the underlying moves.
